claim.qualifier: EPA combined-cycle range for Lucid Air Grand Touring AWD with 19-inch wheels — the longest EPA range of any production EV.
claim.verbatim_quote: Air Grand Touring AWD (big pack) — 516 miles — EPA combined-cycle (19in wheels)

reality.qualifier: Consumer Reports 70 mph test on Lucid Air Grand Touring measured 344 mi vs ~396 mi EPA at the time of test (-52 mi gap). Car and Driver's 75 mph test on a 2022 Grand Touring achieved 410 mi — the longest result in their EV database. Recharged synthesis: typical 70–75 mph range for Grand Touring is 340–390 mi.
reality.verbatim_quote: Car and Driver's 75-mph test has seen an early Grand Touring clear about 410 miles before tapping out, still the longest range they've recorded from any EV.

sources.name: Consumer Reports — Real-World EV Range Comparison (Lucid Air -52 mi gap)
Recharged — Lucid Air Real World Range

narrative_one_liner: Lucid Air GT 516 mi EPA; CR 70 mph test 344 vs 396 EPA-at-time (-52 mi). C/D 75 mph: 410 mi (-21% from 516).
narrative: Lucid advertises 516 mi EPA for the Air Grand Touring AWD with 19-inch wheels — the longest EPA range of any production EV. Consumer Reports' 70 mph test measured 344 mi against 396 mi EPA-at-test-time, a 52-mile gap (tied for largest with F-150 Lightning and Rivian R1S). Car and Driver's 75 mph test on a 2022 Grand Touring measured 410 mi — still the longest result in C/D's EV database, but 21% below the current 516 EPA. The Lucid Air is a long-range leader; even its shortfall puts it ahead of competitors. But the magnitude of the gap from headline number is substantial.
methodology_notes: CR's gap is reported against the EPA value at time of test (~396 mi). Current EPA is 516 mi for 19-inch wheels (raised due to wheel/efficiency updates), so the gap from current advertising is larger than what CR reported.
caveats: Wheel size dramatically affects EPA range: 516 mi (19in) → 469 mi (21in) — a 47-mile wheel-size cliff. See separate wheel_size_cliff record.
Lucid Air offers higher-range trim variants beyond what CR tested.
The 21% gap is computed against the 516 (19in) figure; against the 21in EPA of 469, the gap is 13% (similar to Rivian R1S).
alternative_explanations: Lucid's 900V+ architecture is genuinely efficient; the gap reflects the natural physics of high-speed range loss applied to a long-range claim.
Aerodynamic and tire choices are significantly different in EPA testing vs. C/D 75 mph testing.
